parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no traveler-facing criminalisation, no facility or document restrictions on visitors, and layered protections: anti-discrimination law covering gender identity and expression, hate-crime aggravation, migration-law non-discrimination, and a prison protocol placing trans detainees by identity. Marriage/recourse exists for visitors whose relationship is read as same-sex. Documented anti-trans violence (2023 murder, 2021 group beating) is serious but appears as scattered incidents with confessed perpetrator and litigation/court functioning, not an organised campaign or state targeting. The worst documented feature is tier 4 (dated/scattered incidents) against strong documented protective machinery. The 2024 'regression' assessment and stalled legislation pull slightly downward but no restriction was enacted against visitors. Minors face contested resident-level care policy that does not reach travelling minors directly.

entry_documents.protection: Migration law (2021) bans discrimination on sexual orientation/gender identity; no visitor border restrictions documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents come from home country; no documented mismatch friction at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no arrests of trans visitors reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison protocol: placement by gender identity, segmented housing, medical review; committee oversees trans visitors' access rules.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detention ever occurred, protocol governs placement; institutional accountability bodies appear to operate.

federal_state_facilities.protection: National circulars mandate social-name use in care and schools with gender-identity-respecting bathrooms, sanctionable on non-application.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: 2017 education circular is nationwide; visitor minors travelling with a parent would ordinarily fall under it.

care_services.protection: Public system funds surgery/HRT since 2013; social-name registration circular (2011) applies to all care centres.
care_services.interaction: Minors' hormone initiation deferral circular (2024) and annulled budget bar (2025) are resident-policy conflicts, not visitor exposures; emergency care refusal not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 373 morality provision historically used to harass gay men (dated, pre-2015); no record of current use against trans visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police human-rights department credited with ending reported abuses by 2015; incitement bill passed only lower chamber (unenacted).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Historic police lever weakens over time; current documented enforcement is protective or neutral.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not directly documented for travelling minors; legislative commission (2025) recommends banning minor hormonal treatment and repealing school protections — non-binding.
minors_guardians.protection: Constitutional court annulled budget bar on minors' hormone financing; 2022 law protects LGBTIQA+ minors' right to develop gender identity; LGR for 14-18 via family court; under-14 excluded except per April 2025 inapplicability ruling (single case).
minors_guardians.interaction: School circular covers visitor children; contested care policy creates uncertainty for a guardian seeking continuity of treatment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: 2023 murder of young trans man (killer confessed, no sentence recorded); 2021 hotel beating and captivity of trans man and girlfriend in capital; alleged institutional discrimination against trans police officer (2025).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime aggravation since 2012; 2025 first lesbophobic femicide conviction shows courts acting; civil society actively litigates.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is scattered, not patterned/state-directed; court recourse demonstrated; background rate unknown so frequency unquantifiable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: capital incident lacks recorded sentence; prosecution figures under aggravating circumstance unavailable; no incitement offence enacted; 2024 judged a year of regression amid ultra-right rise.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination law, migration protections, complementary protection against refoulement on SOGI grounds.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Stalled legislation suggests protective drift paused but no operative restriction enacted; visitor recourse runs through courts shown to work.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: no criminalisation, working remedies, brief/incidental friction. Here protections are broader (anti-discrimination, hate-crime aggravation, custody protocol) but two serious violent incidents exceed that anchor's low severity, pulling slightly below or level.

Close match: equality statute, police review, real but occasional street violence with functional courts. This jurisdiction shows a confressed murder (higher severity) but also demonstrated convictions (lesboophobic femicide) and stronger protective machinery — roughly level.

Materially above: that anchor features sporadic ejection, stalled investigations and thin remedies. Here protections are explicitly documented, institutions act on complaints, and no service-denial pattern against trans people is documented.

Below: that anchor has enforcement with prompt apologies/discipline and broad tolerance. Here two emblematic violent attacks, an institutional discrimination suit against police, and a documented political regression prevent reaching that tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines no trans-specific criminalisation, no visitor-facing facility or document restrictions, and layered operative protections: anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, migration non-discrimination, a functioning custody protocol, and courts that convict bias killers. Against this, documented harms are scattered societal violence (one murder with confessed perpetrator, one severe group assault), not organised or state targeting, and their frequency relative to background homicide is unquantified — weighted per rule 16 rather than as a campaign. The 'regression' political climate is a trajectory signal, not yet an operative restriction. Travelling minors encounter protective school circulars and court-backstopped care policy; the contested minors' treatment debate is resident-facing and non-binding. Net: a protective regime with real but episodic violence — mid-to-upper Reduced Risk band.
